title: Reduction of oligomer size modulates the competition between cluster formation and phase separation of the tumor suppressor SPOP.
authors: Sabri, Nafiseh; Cuneo, Matthew J; Marzahn, Melissa R; Lee, Jihun; Bouchard, Jill J; Gullulu, Omer; Vaithiyalingam, Sivaraja; Borgia, Madeleine B; Schmit, Jeremy; Mittag, Tanja
one_liner_zh: 该文研究肿瘤抑制因子SPOP的寡聚化突变如何调控其与底物DAXX的凝聚体形成与泛素化活性，聚焦IDR介导的PPI与相分离机制，但方法以实验为主，缺乏AI或物理模拟建模。
abstract: Phase separation compartmentalizes many cellular pathways. Given that the same interactions that drive phase separation mediate the formation of soluble complexes below the saturation concentration, the contribution of condensates versus complexes to function is sometimes unclear. Here, we characterized several new cancer-associated mutations of the tumor suppressor speckle-type POZ protein (SPOP), a substrate recognition subunit of the Cullin3-RING ubiquitin ligase. This pointed to a strategy for generating separation-of-function mutations. SPOP self-associates into linear oligomers and interacts with multivalent substrates, and this mediates the formation of condensates. These condensates bear the hallmarks of enzymatic ubiquitination activity. We characterized the effect of mutations in the dimerization domains of SPOP on its linear oligomerization, binding to its substrate DAXX, and phase separation with DAXX. We showed that the mutations reduce SPOP oligomerization and shift the size distribution of SPOP oligomers to smaller sizes. The mutations therefore reduce the binding affinity to DAXX but unexpectedly enhance the poly-ubiquitination activity of SPOP toward DAXX. Enhanced activity may be explained by enhanced phase separation of DAXX with the SPOP mutants. Our results provide a comparative assessment of the functional role of complexes versus condensates and support a model in which phase separation is an important factor in SPOP function. Our findings also suggest that tuning of linear SPOP self-association could be used by the cell to modulate activity and provide insights into the mechanisms underlying hypermorphic SPOP mutations. The characteristics of cancer-associated SPOP mutations suggest a route for designing separation-of-function mutations in other phase-separating systems.
abstract_zh: 相分离（phase separation）将许多细胞通路分隔开来。鉴于驱动相分离的相同相互作用在低于饱和浓度时介导可溶性复合物的形成，凝聚体与复合物对功能的贡献有时并不明确。在此，我们表征了肿瘤抑制因子斑点型POZ蛋白（SPOP）的几个新癌症相关突变，SPOP是Cullin3-RING泛素连接酶的底物识别亚基。这指向了一种生成功能分离突变的策略。SPOP自组装成线性寡聚体，并与多价底物相互作用，这介导了凝聚体的形成。这些凝聚体具有酶促泛素化活性的特征。我们表征了SPOP二聚化结构域中的突变对其线性寡聚化、与其底物DAXX的结合以及与DAXX的相分离的影响。我们表明，这些突变减少了SPOP的寡聚化，并将SPOP寡聚体的尺寸分布转向更小的尺寸。因此，这些突变降低了对DAXX的结合亲和力，但出乎意料地增强了SPOP对DAXX的多聚泛素化活性。增强的活性可能通过DAXX与SPOP突变体的增强相分离来解释。我们的结果提供了复合物与凝聚体功能作用的比较评估，并支持一个模型，即相分离是SPOP功能的重要因素。我们的发现还表明，细胞可能通过调节SPOP线性自关联来调节活性，并为超形态SPOP突变背后的机制提供了见解。癌症相关SPOP突变的特征提示了在其他相分离系统中设计功能分离突变的一条途径。
